result.title: Evidence or Marginal? What Moment-Vector Propagation Computes in Polynomial Density Neurons
result.summary: When a neuron's input is lost, or known through a belief $q$, what should it output? For a neuron storing a joint polynomial density $N$ with input density $D$, two formulas compete. $p_\mathrm{CD}=E_q[N]/E_q[D]$ costs one matrix-vector product; Hierarchical Correlation Reconstruction introduces it as a constant-denominator approximation to $p_\mathrm{EU}=E_q[N/D]$. For a density model both are exact answers to different questions: $p_\mathrm{CD}$ is Bayesian updating with the belief as virtual evidence; $p_\mathrm{EU}$ installs the belief as a new marginal (Jeffrey's rule). With a missing input $p_\mathrm{CD}$ returns the model's conditional; $p_\mathrm{EU}$ generally does not. This post hoc reading is proved, and illustrated outside the pair family up to $k=8$ inputs; it has no pre-registered test, only one exploratory real-data pilot. Post hoc, closed forms fall within a factor 2 of all 112 measured gaps, and negative density begins near input correlation $1/k$. In a pre-registered synthetic study (up to 32 inputs), 5 of 15 hypotheses are supported, 2 inconclusive and 8 not supported, including all three on transfer beyond equicorrelated Gaussians. Post hoc, where $p_\mathrm{EU}$ is defined, truncation usually outweighs the gap for Beta beliefs in pair neurons; triple neurons under flat and data beliefs are exceptions.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究多项式密度神经元在输入缺失或以信念 q 已知时应输出什么，比较两种公式：p_CD=E_q[N]/E_q[D]（把信念当作虚拟证据做贝叶斯更新）与 p_EU=E_q[N/D]（把信念作为新边缘，即 Jeffrey 规则），并以后验解读、合成与前导实验检验二者差异与适用边界。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“条件化 vs 替换边缘”的形式区分可能为 LVR 中“答案是否真正使用视觉证据、抑或绕开证据走边缘旁路”提供一种可核查的信念状态更新刻画，但对象为密度神经元、无视觉与语言实验，迁移需较多核查。
